english.title: Use violence / threats / a form of coercion to cause another person to enter into a marriage

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: anti social behaviour crime and policing act 2014

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) used violence, threats or a form of coercion for the purpose of causing another person, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..), to enter into a marriage,

(A)_[believing]_
(B)_[and you ought reasonably have believed]_

that your conduct may have caused them to enter into the marriage without free and full consent
english.legislation: Contrary to section 121(1) and (9) of the Anti-social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014.

english.notes:
(i)This is also a preventative offence so it covers a scenario where a person is subjected to threats or violence with the aim or purpose of causing them to enter into marriage, so for example where a person is assaulted with the intention of forcing them to enter into a forced marriage. An offence is committed whether or not the forced marriage goes ahead.
(ii) In relation to a victim who lacks capacity to consent to marriage, the offence is capable of being committed by any conduct carried out for the purpose of causing the victim to enter into a marriage (whether or not the conduct amounts to violence, threats or any other form coercion).
(iii) 'Marriage' means any religious or civil ceremony of marriage (whether or not legally binding).
(iv) It is irrelevant whether the conduct (violence, threats, coercion) is directed at the victim of the offence or another person.
(v) A person commits an offence only if, at the time of the conduct -(a) the person or the victim or both of them are in England or Wales,
(b) neither the person nor the victim is in England or Wales but at least one of them is habitually resident in England and Wales, or
(c) neither the person nor the victim is in the United Kingdom but at least one of them is a UK national

other.penalty:
Summary: Twelve months imprisonment and / or a fine
Indictment: Seven years imprisonment and / or a fine

Important Note:
In relation to an offence committed before paragraph 24(2) of Schedule 22 to the Sentencing Act 2020 comes into force (01/12/20), the reference to 12 months imprisonment in relation to summary offences, above, is to be read as a reference to 6 months imprisonment.
